name: Carrow Thermal Henley
description:
A three-button henley cut from a dense cotton-polyester thermal weave, double-stitched at every stress point and pre-washed until the fabric has the soft, slightly pilled texture of something that's already survived a winter. Available in four colors: slate, rust, off-white, and a dark green that Carrow calls 'Fen.' The collar sits just high enough to layer under a jacket without bunching. The cuffs are ribbed and wide enough to accommodate most basic forearm augments without rolling up.

Carrow is a Tier 2 workhorse label out of what used to be Milwaukee's industrial west side — they make clothes for people who stand outside in November. The henley has been in their catalog for eleven years with almost no changes. That's the point. Dock workers, transit mechanics, warehouse supervisors, and anyone who needs a shirt that doesn't ask anything of them wear this. It just works.
what_it_says: You're practical, unpretentious, and you've been cold before. No performance, no statement — just someone who picks the right tool for the job and moves on.
story_hooks: A specific run of Carrow Thermal Henleys from 2197 was accidentally dyed with a batch of pigment that contains trace amounts of a restricted industrial solvent — long-term skin absorption is causing nerve numbness in some wearers, and Carrow is quietly trying to buy back the affected units before anyone files a claim.

A transit union organizer uses the Carrow Henley as an informal identifier — anyone showing up to a clandestine meeting wearing one is presumed sympathetic, a system that's worked until someone started wearing them who definitely isn't.
A character finds a Carrow Henley in a deceased relative's belongings, the cuffs still faintly stained with something they can't identify.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian henley with masculine, approachable silhouette. The three-button placket sits centered on the chest, lending a casual-but-intentional quality. The fabric drapes with slight body-conforming ease—not tight, not loose. Visual weight concentrated in the torso; shoulders sit naturally without architectural padding.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed athletic—enough room through the chest and shoulders for layering or augment accommodation, but tapered slightly at the waist to prevent excess fabric. The sleeve length hits mid-forearm, intentionally designed to clear wrist-level tech. Not oversized, not slim; precisely calibrated for function.
physical_description.primary_material: Dense cotton-polyester thermal weave blend. High thread count for durability; the poly content provides moisture-wicking and structural integrity through repeated washing.
physical_description.texture: Soft with controlled pilling—the 'pre-weathered' surface shows micro-texture and subtle nap variation. Not rough, but not smooth. Tactilely honest: this is a fabric that's been broken in and is ready for work.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary offering in slate (neutral gray-blue), rust (industrial orange-brown), off-white (cream with warmth), and Fen (forest green with slight gray undertone). All colorways have muted saturation—nothing pops or draws unnecessary attention.
physical_description.closures: Three-button placket; buttons appear to be polymer or coated metal, color-matched to garment. Simple, functional, no branding on closures.
distinctive_features: Ribbed cuffs wide enough to accommodate forearm augments without constraint
High collar designed to layer cleanly under jackets without bunching
No visible branding or logos; manufacturer name present only on interior tag
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2—quality workwear. Not luxury, not disposable. Built for people earning steady wages in physical labor sectors.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals reliability, pragmatism, and honest work. Worn by dock workers, maintenance techs, transit operators, warehouse supervisors—anyone for whom clothing is equipment, not expression. Indicates Milwaukee industrial heritage; appeals to labor-forward identity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually broken-in within first season. Slight pilling develops naturally; this is expected and acceptable. After years of wear, fades unevenly in high-contact areas (collar, cuffs, chest button area). Stitching remains solid. Appears most authentic when worn, not pristine.

image_prompt: A Carrow Thermal Henley in slate color, worn on a tired-looking model with visible forearm augmentation (chrome wrist unit peeking from under the henley's generous cuff). Standing in the amber-sodium light of an early morning industrial dock in Milwaukee; concrete and steel shipping containers in soft focus behind. The henley's three buttons partially undone, collar naturally creased from being layered under a jacket. Soft morning fog diffuses the harsh light. The fabric's subtle texture and pilling visible in close detail. Slight sweat marks at the collar from honest work. Model's expression neutral, looking away from camera—this is not a pose, it's a pause. Moody, utilitarian, authentic documentation rather than fashion glamour. --ar 2:3 --v 6
